description: The migration runner (Go `core/upgrade.Migrator`) against a recording driver. Each scenario registers `migrations`, adds `drivers` in order and runs `steps` on one migrator with target `target`. A driver reports `version` until `set_version` succeeds; a `*_fail` field makes that driver call fail with that message. A migration with `fail` fails its Up with that message; `down` gives it a Down, `down_fail` a failing one. `backups` creates backup directories before the first step. `calls` is what the step did, in order: `<schema> backup|restore <backup dir name>`, `<schema> up|down <version>`, `<schema> set_version <version>`. `history` is cumulative; `versions` is each schema's version file (`""` when absent); `backups` lists each schema's backup directories by name after the step. `error` is the exact error text, or null. Each migration may also carry `verify` (a passing verify step) or `verify_fail`, and `cancel` cancels the run's context after its Up. A scenario may set `final_verify` or `final_verify_fail` (the migrator's final verify), `data_dir` (an explicit data dir instead of XDG), `registry: own` with `default_migrations` (registered in the default registry, which an own registry must not see) and `locked_backups` (old backups that cannot be removed). A step may set `canceled` (run with a canceled context). Calls also log `<schema> verify <version>` and `<schema> final_verify <version>`. `events` lists what the run published, in order, under the default topics; `duration_ms` is left out of the payloads (runners check it is a non-negative integer where present). `warnings` lists, as prefixes, what the run logged.
